findings.passage: There are no protections in the resolution, there is no future proofing for when biometric and virtual IDs become safer.
findings.note: Release on Senate passage of S.J.R. 10, the photo-ID-to-vote constitutional amendment. He says it lacks protection for future ID technology.

findings.passage: All of these amendments were tabled.
findings.note: Same release. Refers to amendments offered on acceptable ID types, free state IDs, same-day registration and provisional ballots; all were tabled.

findings.passage: House Bill 472 was originally a bipartisan bill to help Ohioans experiencing homelessness get free identifying documents like birth certificates or state IDs.
findings.note: Release on Senate passage of Sub. H.B. 472, amended to require mail voters to send a photocopy of ID or upload it when requesting a ballot. He describes the bill's original purpose.

findings.passage: It would be comical if it weren't so harmful.
findings.note: Same release, his statement on the mail-ballot ID amendment to H.B. 472.

findings.passage: ‘This bullshit bill is just another horrific attempt to further disenfranchise Ohioans who want to participate in the political process,’ said DeMora.
findings.note: Release on his no vote on S.B. 293 (ends the grace period for mailed ballots to arrive). Related election-law item, not an ID item.

findings.passage: Aside from disenfranchising thousands of people every year, now this bill will make it so any mistake on any database will mean you are kicked off the voter rolls.
findings.note: Release on his no vote on the House changes to S.B. 293, which added voter-roll matching from S.B. 153. Related voter-roll item.

findings.passage: It will be Ohioans who will suffer from this decision.
findings.note: Release on the Secretary of State's decision to send the statewide voter file to the federal Justice Department. Related voter-roll item.
